title: PostgreSQL as AstraVector source of truth

blocks.heading: Canonical state
blocks.text: PostgreSQL remains the canonical source of truth for AstraVector document versions, chunks, vector bindings and lifecycle status.

blocks.heading: Projection rule
blocks.text: Qdrant is a derived projection and must be repaired from PostgreSQL when drift is detected.

blocks.heading: Visibility recheck
blocks.text: RetrieveContext must perform a final PostgreSQL visibility recheck before returning contexts to callers.

blocks.heading: Mutation discipline
blocks.text: Lifecycle mutations must update PostgreSQL first and then publish projection events through the outbox.

blocks.heading: Audit fields
blocks.text: Production troubleshooting relies on document_id, document_version, access_zone_id and lifecycle_status metadata.

title: Qdrant projection and payload index policy

blocks.heading: Payload index purpose
blocks.text: Qdrant payload indexes reduce filtered vector search latency for access_zone_id, lifecycle_status, access_level and expires_at_epoch filters.

blocks.heading: Tenant filter
blocks.text: The access_zone_id payload index is mandatory because every retrieval query filters by tenant zone.

blocks.heading: Lifecycle filter
blocks.text: The lifecycle_status and expires_at_epoch payload indexes protect retrieval from deleted or expired points.

blocks.heading: Representation filter
blocks.text: Model version, tokenizer version, dense_version and sparse_version payload fields keep incompatible vectors out of search results.

blocks.heading: Repair payload
blocks.text: Reconciliation must rebuild Qdrant payloads with the same fields used by normal outbox upserts.

title: Vector outbox lifecycle and failure handling

blocks.heading: Claim
blocks.text: The vector outbox worker claims pending events before sending upsert or delete operations to Qdrant.

blocks.heading: Retry
blocks.text: Temporary Qdrant failures move the event to retry pending with a later next_attempt_at timestamp.

blocks.heading: Dead letter
blocks.text: Permanent failures move outbox events to a dead-letter state for operator review.

blocks.heading: Fencing
blocks.text: Operation version fencing prevents stale outbox events from overwriting newer vector binding state.

blocks.heading: Staleness
blocks.text: Outbox staleness measures the time between event creation and successful projection processing.

blocks.heading: Scan
blocks.text: Reconciliation scans PostgreSQL vector bindings and compares them with Qdrant points.

blocks.heading: Missing point
blocks.text: If a binding is active but the Qdrant point is missing, reconciliation rebuilds the vector payload and upserts the point.

blocks.heading: Orphan point
blocks.text: If a Qdrant point has no active PostgreSQL binding and no legal hold protection, reconciliation can delete the orphan point.

blocks.heading: Legal hold skip
blocks.text: Reconciliation must skip legal hold points even when their TTL has expired.

blocks.heading: Metrics
blocks.text: Reconciliation reports scanned, repaired, skipped and error counts for production dashboards.

title: TTL cleanup and legal hold lifecycle

blocks.heading: Expiration
blocks.text: Expired documents without legal hold must be hidden from retrieval after the configured expiration time.

blocks.heading: Legal hold
blocks.text: A legal hold prevents TTL cleanup from deleting protected documents even when expiration time has passed.

blocks.heading: Delete pending
blocks.text: TTL cleanup moves eligible bindings to DELETE_PENDING before Qdrant delete is attempted.

blocks.heading: Permanent failure
blocks.text: Repeated deletion failures can lead to DELETE_PERMANENTLY_FAILED for operator investigation.

blocks.heading: Purge safety
blocks.text: Tombstone purge must not remove bindings while live outbox events still exist.

title: Gateway trust and forwarded identity headers

blocks.heading: Trusted gateway
blocks.text: AstraVector trusts x-astravector-role only when a configured gateway trust proof is present.

blocks.heading: Header stripping
blocks.text: The gateway must strip user-supplied x-astravector-* headers before forwarding requests.

blocks.heading: Network policy
blocks.text: Kubernetes NetworkPolicy should allow gRPC ingress only from trusted gateway pods.

blocks.heading: mTLS recommendation
blocks.text: Production deployments should combine gateway trust headers with mTLS or service mesh identity.

blocks.heading: Direct access risk
blocks.text: If the service is exposed directly, a client could forge role metadata without gateway enforcement.

blocks.heading: Readiness
blocks.text: Readiness should become true only after PostgreSQL ping and Qdrant collection checks succeed.

blocks.heading: Liveness
blocks.text: Liveness verifies the gRPC server process is alive but does not replace dependency readiness checks.

blocks.heading: Shutdown
blocks.text: During graceful shutdown the service sets readiness false before cancelling background workers.

blocks.heading: Drain
blocks.text: The shutdown drain window gives outbox, recovery and retention workers time to stop safely.

blocks.heading: Probe failure
blocks.text: If Qdrant is unreachable during startup, readiness must not advertise the service as ready.

blocks.heading: Purpose
blocks.text: Quality Bench verifies retrieval quality, access isolation, GraphRAG contribution, MMR diversity and negative query behavior.

blocks.heading: Static mode
blocks.text: When no endpoint is configured, Quality Bench performs static fixture validation and marks runtime execution as skipped.

blocks.heading: Remote mode
blocks.text: When ASTRAVECTOR_QUALITY_ENDPOINT is set, Quality Bench calls RetrieveContext over gRPC and evaluates golden queries.

blocks.heading: Reports
blocks.text: Quality Bench writes quality-report.json, quality-report.md, failures.jsonl and candidates.jsonl.

blocks.heading: Gate
blocks.text: The quick profile is intended for PR checks while production-candidate uses stricter thresholds for release branches.
